newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 31.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Managing director of Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Company, Sam Jonah, leads a delegation to Ivory Coast to seek gold exploration permits and discuss other forms of cooperation.

- Liberia's president elect, Charles Taylor, who launched a civil war from Ivory Coast in 1989, visits Ivorian president Henri Konan Bedie, expresses regret over war casualties and vows to promote a lasting peace in his country.

- Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan, presiding over a meeting on helping small businesses develop by improving government bureaucracy, denounces "absenteeism, lateness, administrative delays and corruption" by staff in public bodies.
- World Health Organsisation attends meeting to discuss regional strategy on use of refrigerants harmful to the world's ozone layer.

- Japanese cooperation agency funds to Ivory Coast since 1980 total 153 billion CFA francs. Recent projects include a new fishing terminal at the second port of San Pedro, a training institute for promotion of mechanisation of farming, and hospital renovations.

- Ivory Coast and the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation sign a $257,000 deal on improving water management and securing supplies to farmers, particularlly in the central Bandama river basin which contains the country's largest hydrolectric dam.
- Government attempts to chase illegal farmers out of protected forests are hampered by the involvement of some local officials.

- Around 22,000 second-hand cars, nicknamed "Goodbye Frances", have been imported into Ivory Coast since import rules were relaxed in January 1996, slowing a recovery in new car sales following the 1994 devaluation of the country's CFA franc currency.
